definition_zh: 细胞核；原子核；核心
definition_en: the central part of a cell or atom, or the core of a group or object
core_image: 一个果核：坚硬的小圆体，所有东西都围着它转
scene: 细胞核里装着它的大部分遗传物质。The nucleus of a cell contains most of its DNA.
sceneCN: 这里 nucleus 指「细胞核」（第 1 个义项：细胞内保存 DNA 的中央结构）；句意：细胞核保存着细胞的大部分 DNA；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 细胞核；原子核；核心；中心部分；神经核；（音节的）核

forms.label: 果核义（拉丁本义，现代英语少用）

derivatives.zh: 核的；原子核的；细胞核的

senses.title: Cell nucleus
senses.definition: the membrane-bound organelle that contains most of a cell's DNA
senses.definitionCN: 细胞中含有大部分 DNA 的膜结合细胞器
senses.example: The nucleus of a human cell holds twenty-three pairs of chromosomes.
senses.exampleCN: 人类细胞的细胞核里有二十三对染色体。
senses.why: The biological sense was named after the kernel of a nut: a small central body around which the rest is arranged.
senses.whyCN: 生物学义按坚果的果核命名：一个居中的小体，其余部分围绕它安排。

senses.title: Atomic nucleus
senses.definition: the dense central core of an atom, made of protons and neutrons
senses.definitionCN: 原子中由质子与中子构成的致密中心
senses.example: The nucleus of carbon-12 contains six protons and six neutrons.
senses.exampleCN: 碳-12 的原子核含有六个质子和六个中子。
senses.why: Physics reused the kernel image for the tiny centre of an atom, because almost all its mass sits there.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把果核意象用于原子的微小中心，因为原子几乎全部质量都在那里。

senses.title: Core of a group
senses.definition: the central group of people around whom a larger body forms
senses.definitionCN: 较大群体围绕其形成的核心人群
senses.example: A small nucleus of volunteers kept the project alive.
senses.exampleCN: 一小群志愿者构成的核心让项目维持下去。
senses.why: A group with a hard centre and looser edges matches the kernel image, so the word serves for social structure as well.
senses.whyCN: 一个有坚硬核心与松散边缘的群体符合果核意象，因此这个词也用于社会结构。

senses.title: Central part of an object
senses.definition: the central mass of a comet, crystal or other object
senses.definitionCN: 彗星、晶体或其它物体的中心团块
senses.example: The comet's nucleus is a dirty ball of ice and rock.
senses.exampleCN: 彗核是一个由冰与岩石组成的脏雪球。
senses.why: The word generalises from the kernel to any object's central solid part.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从果核泛化，指任何物体中心那个坚实的部分。

senses.title: Brain nucleus
senses.definition: a cluster of nerve cells in the brain or spinal cord
senses.definitionCN: 脑或脊髓中一簇神经细胞
senses.example: The nucleus accumbens is linked to reward.
senses.exampleCN: 伏隔核与奖赏有关。
senses.why: Anatomists saw clustered cell bodies as kernels inside the nervous tissue, and named them accordingly.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学家把聚在一起的细胞体看作神经组织里的果核，于是如此命名。

senses.title: Syllable nucleus
senses.definition: the vowel or vowel-like sound that forms the centre of a syllable
senses.definitionCN: 构成音节中心的元音或类元音
senses.example: In the word 'cat', the vowel is the syllable nucleus.
senses.exampleCN: 在 cat 这个词里，元音就是音节核。
senses.why: Linguists borrowed the word for the part every syllable must have at its centre, with consonants around it.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家借用这个词，指每个音节中心必须具备的成分，辅音围绕它排列。

senses.title: Galactic nucleus
senses.definition: the dense central region of a galaxy
senses.definitionCN: 星系中央的致密区域
senses.example: The galactic nucleus glows with billions of old stars.
senses.exampleCN: 星系核因数十亿颗老年恒星而发光。
senses.why: Astronomy applies the kernel image at the largest scale, where mass and light concentrate at the centre.
senses.whyCN: 天文学把果核意象用到最大尺度，那里质量与光都集中在中心。

senses.title: Nucleation centre
senses.definition: a small particle or site where a new phase begins to form
senses.definitionCN: 新相开始形成的小颗粒或位点
senses.example: Dust provides the nuclei on which cloud droplets condense.
senses.exampleCN: 尘埃提供了云滴凝结所需的核。
senses.why: A growing crystal or droplet needs a seed at its centre, and the word names that starting point.
senses.whyCN: 生长中的晶体或液滴需要中心的一个种子，这个词就命名那个起点。

senses.title: Nucleus of a collection
senses.definition: the original small set of items around which a larger collection grows
senses.definitionCN: 较大收藏围绕其生长的最初那一小批藏品
senses.example: Six paintings formed the nucleus of the museum's collection.
senses.exampleCN: 六幅画构成了这家博物馆藏品的核心。
senses.why: The kernel image extends to collections: a small hard core of founding items attracts more around it.
senses.whyCN: 果核意象延伸到收藏：一小批创始藏品构成坚硬的核心，吸引更多东西围绕它聚集。

intro.en: Nucleus is Latin for a nut's kernel; science then applied the little central body to cells, atoms, brains and galaxies.
intro.cn: nucleus 在拉丁语里指坚果的果核；科学随后把这个居中的小体用于细胞、原子、脑与星系。

items.en: Latin nux, with the stem nuc-, meant a nut. Its diminutive nucleus meant the small kernel inside a shell.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nux（词干 nuc-）指坚果。其指小形式 nucleus 指壳内的小果仁。

items.en: Nucleus kept the physical sense of a kernel, and by extension any hard central part. English borrowed it in the 17th century.
items.cn: nucleus 保留了果仁的具体意义，并引申指任何坚硬的中心部分。英语在 17 世纪借入。

items.en: Robert Brown described a small body inside plant cells and called it the nucleus in 1831, a term generally credited to him.
items.cn: Robert Brown 在 1831 年描述植物细胞内的一个小体并称之为 nucleus，这一术语一般认为出自他。

items.en: After Rutherford's scattering experiments, the dense centre of the atom was called the nucleus. The date is approximate, around 1911 to 1912.
items.cn: 卢瑟福散射实验之后，原子的致密中心被称为 nucleus。年代约为 1911 至 1912 年。

items.en: The word spread to astronomy, neuroanatomy and linguistics, always keeping the shape of a centre with surrounding parts.
items.cn: 这个词扩散到天文学、神经解剖学与语言学，始终保留「中心加周围部分」的形状。

note.en: The first group separates nucleus from the adjective and from the smaller body inside it; the second separates it from general words for a centre.
note.cn: 第一组把 nucleus 与它的形容词以及它内部更小的结构分开；第二组把它与泛指的「中心」词分开。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of a nucleus'; it is used in nuclear physics and nuclear envelope, while nucleus is the countable noun.
entries.definitionCN: 是形容词，意为「核的」，用于核物理与核膜等；nucleus 是可数名词。

entries.definition: A small structure within the cell nucleus where ribosomes are assembled; it is not the nucleus itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指细胞核内组装核糖体的小结构，不是细胞核本身。

entries.definition: The building block of DNA and RNA; it shares the nuc- root through the idea of a core, but names a molecule.
entries.definitionCN: 指 DNA 与 RNA 的构件；它通过「核心」的观念共享 nuc- 词根，但指的是分子。

entries.definition: The central part of anything, often of an apple or the earth; it is the everyday synonym of nucleus outside science.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何事物的中心部分，常见于苹果核或地核；是 nucleus 在科学之外的日常同义词。

entries.definition: The middle point or area of a space; it describes position, not a distinct body with surrounding parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指空间的中心点或区域，描述位置，而不是一个带周围部分的独立小体。

entries.definition: The edible part inside a nut, and the literal sense behind nucleus; it is also used figuratively for the essence of a matter.
entries.definitionCN: 指坚果内的可食部分，是 nucleus 背后的字面义；也比喻事情的要点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: nucleus is Latin for a nut's kernel: the hard thing in the middle.
normal.cn: nucleus 是拉丁语的「果仁」：中间那个硬东西。

normal.en: The family runs nuclear, nucleolus, nucleated, enucleate and nucleation.
normal.cn: 同族词有 nuclear、nucleolus、nucleated、enucleate、nucleation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: cell nucleus, atomic nucleus, comet nucleus, syllable nucleus.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：细胞核、原子核、彗核、音节核。

normal.en: The plural is nuclei, not nucleuses, in scientific writing.
normal.cn: 科学写作中复数用 nuclei，而不用 nucleuses。

normal.en: Every use keeps the same picture: a centre with a surrounding body.
normal.cn: 每个用法都保留同一幅图：一个中心加一个围绕它的整体。

abstract.en: Picture a peach: the stone is the nucleus, the flesh is everything that surrounds it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只桃子：桃核是 nucleus，果肉是围绕它的一切。

abstract.en: An atom is a tiny solar system with the nucleus as its sun.
abstract.cn: 原子像一个微型太阳系，原子核就是它的太阳。

abstract.en: A nucleus of volunteers is a seed crystal around which a project forms.
abstract.cn: 志愿者的核心就是一颗种子晶体，项目围绕它生长。

examples.en: The nucleus stores the cell's chromosomes and controls gene expression.
examples.cn: 细胞核储存细胞的染色体并控制基因表达。

examples.en: Protons and neutrons occupy the atomic nucleus.
examples.cn: 质子与中子占据原子核。

examples.en: A small nucleus of supporters organised the campaign.
examples.cn: 一小群支持者构成的核心组织了这场运动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nucleus 就是果核」→ 中间那个核 → 细胞核、原子核、核心

root: 拉丁语 nux（坚果，词干 nuc-）→ 指小形式 nucleus「果仁、小核」→ 英语 nucleus；细胞核义始于 1831 年 Robert Brown，原子核义约始于 1911 年。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses keep one shape: a compact centre surrounded by a larger body. The kernel becomes a cell organelle, an atomic core, a group of people, a comet's heart, a brain cluster, a syllable's vowel, a galactic centre, a seed crystal, and finally the founding core of a collection.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项保持同一种形状：一个紧凑的中心，被更大的整体包围。果仁先后变成细胞器、原子核心、人群核心、彗星中心、脑内细胞簇、音节元音、星系中心、成核种子，最后成为一批藏品围绕其生长的收藏核心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard kernel at the centre, with everything else arranged around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：中央一颗坚硬的果核，其余一切都围着它安排。

branches.en: THE TWO SCIENTIFIC CENTRES: the organelle that holds DNA, and the dense core of the atom.
branches.cn: 两个科学中心：保存 DNA 的细胞器，以及原子的致密核心。

branches.en: SOCIAL AND PHYSICAL CORES: a founding group, and the solid centre of a comet or crystal.
branches.cn: 社会与物理核心：一个创始群体，以及彗星或晶体的坚实中心。

branches.en: ANATOMY AND ASTRONOMY: clustered nerve cells, and the centre of a galaxy.
branches.cn: 解剖与天文：聚成一团的神经细胞，以及星系的中心。

branches.en: LINGUISTICS: the vowel at the centre of a syllable.
branches.cn: 语言学：音节中心的元音。

branches.en: SEED AND SOURCE: the site where growth starts, and the founding core of a collection.
branches.cn: 种子与本源：生长开始的位点，以及一批藏品围绕其生长的收藏核心。

intro.en: Nucleus is a Latin diminutive with no prefix; its family is built with -ar, -olus and -ation.
intro.cn: nucleus 是拉丁语指小词，不带前缀；其词族由 -ar、-olus、-ation 等构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin nux and its diminutive nucleus supply the root. The adjective nuclear adds -ar; nucleolus is a further diminutive; nucleation adds -ation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nux 及其指小形式 nucleus 提供词根。形容词 nuclear 加 -ar；nucleolus 是再一层指小；nucleation 加 -ation。

items.example: The nucleus is bounded by a membrane.
items.exampleCN: 细胞核由一层膜包围。

items.example: Nuclear fission releases energy.
items.exampleCN: 核裂变释放能量。

items.meaning: a small body inside the nucleus
items.example: The nucleolus assembles ribosomes.
items.exampleCN: 核仁组装核糖体。

items.example: Nucleated cells are larger than bacteria.
items.exampleCN: 有核细胞比细菌大。

items.example: The researchers enucleated the egg.
items.exampleCN: 研究者去除了卵细胞的核。

items.meaning: the formation of a first small centre
items.example: Nucleation starts when the liquid cools.
items.exampleCN: 液体冷却时成核开始。

items.meaning: the building block of nucleic acids
items.example: Each nucleotide carries a base.
items.exampleCN: 每个核苷酸携带一个碱基。

items.meaning: relating to the nucleus, used in nucleic acid
items.example: Nucleic acids store genetic information.
items.exampleCN: 核酸储存遗传信息。

items.example: Karyotype pictures the whole nucleus.
items.exampleCN: 核型图展示整个细胞核。

definition_zh: 分子；分数线上方的数；除法中的被除数；比率中的前项
definition_en: the number above the line in a fraction, or the quantity that is divided by another
core_image: 一张纸上写着分数，横线上方的数字被红笔描了一道
scene: 纸上写着一个分数，横线上方的数字被红笔描了一道。In the fraction, the numerator tells how many parts are counted.
sceneCN: 这里 numerator 指「分数中写在横线上方的数，表示取了多少份」（第 1 个义项：分数的分子）；句意为在这个分数里，分子说明数了几份。图中可辨识物件：纸、分数横线、红笔、上下两个数字。

pos.zh: 分子；被除数；比的前项

derivatives.zh: 数字；数字的（同出拉丁 numerus）
数字的；数值的（同出拉丁 numerus）
计算；识数的（同出拉丁 numerare）
列举；清点（同出拉丁 enumerare）

senses.title: The number above the fraction bar
senses.definition: the number in a fraction that shows how many equal parts are taken
senses.definitionCN: 分数中说明取了多少个等份的那个数
senses.example: In the fraction, the numerator tells how many parts are counted.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个分数里，分子说明数了几份。
senses.why: numerator is Latin for 'counter': the top number counts the parts that the fraction is talking about.
senses.whyCN: numerator 在拉丁语里是「数数者」：上面那个数负责清点这个分数所说的份数。

senses.title: The dividend in a division
senses.definition: the quantity that is divided by another quantity
senses.definitionCN: 被另一个量所除的那个量
senses.example: In the written division, the numerator sits inside the bracket.
senses.exampleCN: 在竖式除法里，被除数写在除号里面。
senses.why: a fraction is a division written down, so the top number plays exactly the role of the dividend.
senses.whyCN: 分数就是写下来的除法，因此上面那个数扮演的正是被除数的角色。

senses.title: The first term of a ratio
senses.definition: the first quantity named when two amounts are compared as a ratio
senses.definitionCN: 两个量作比时先说出的那个量
senses.example: In the ratio, the numerator is the part being compared to the whole.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个比里，前项是被拿去与整体比较的那一部分。
senses.why: a ratio is a fraction in words, so the first term takes the place of the top number.
senses.whyCN: 比就是用文字说出的分数，因此前项占据的就是上面那个数的位置。

senses.title: The count in a rate
senses.titleCN: 比率中实际计数的部分
senses.definition: the number of events counted in the top part of a rate or proportion
senses.definitionCN: 比率或比例中，上半部分实际数出的事件数
senses.example: The numerator of the infection rate is the number of new cases.
senses.exampleCN: 感染率的分子是新病例的数目。
senses.why: in public health a rate is written as events over population, and the events are literally the counted numerator.
senses.whyCN: 在公共卫生里，率写成「事件数除以人口数」，事件数就是被数出来的分子。

senses.title: The numerator polynomial
senses.titleCN: 代数分式的分子多项式
senses.definition: the polynomial written above the line in an algebraic fraction
senses.definitionCN: 代数分式中写在横线上方的那个多项式
senses.example: Factor the numerator polynomial before simplifying the expression.
senses.exampleCN: 化简表达式之前，先把分子多项式因式分解。
senses.why: algebraic fractions copy ordinary fractions exactly, so the top polynomial keeps the name of the top number.
senses.whyCN: 代数分式完全照搬普通分数，因此上面那个多项式沿用上面那个数的名字。

senses.title: A common numerator
senses.definition: a numerator shared by two or more fractions after they are adjusted for comparison
senses.definitionCN: 两个或更多分数在调整以便比较后所共有的分子
senses.example: Rewriting both fractions with a common numerator made the larger one obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 把两个分数都改写成相同的分子后，较大的那个就一目了然了。
senses.why: just as fractions can share a denominator, they can be rewritten to share a numerator, and the counting role gives the name.
senses.whyCN: 正如分数可以有公分母，它们也能改写成共同的分子，命名依据仍是「数份」这个角色。

senses.title: The numerator of a percentage
senses.definition: the amount placed over one hundred when a proportion is written as a percentage
senses.definitionCN: 把比例写成百分数时，放在一百上面的那个量
senses.example: In the percentage, the numerator is the share and the denominator is one hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 在百分数里，分子是所占的份额，分母是一百。
senses.why: a percentage is a fraction with one hundred underneath, so the share above the line is still the numerator.
senses.whyCN: 百分数就是分母为一百的分数，因此横线上方的份额仍然是分子。

senses.title: An older word for a counter
senses.definition: an older use for a person who numbers or counts things
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指给事物编号或清点事物的人
senses.example: The old ledger lists the numerator who checked each crate.
senses.exampleCN: 旧账本上记着负责清点每个木箱的人。
senses.why: the Latin agent noun meant 'one who counts', and the mathematical use grew out of that literal counting person.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁施动名词本意是「数数的人」，数学用法正是从那个字面意义上的清点者长出来的。

intro.en: Numerator is Latin numerator 'a counter', from numerare 'to count', from numerus 'number'. The mathematical use came through French numérateur in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: numerator 是拉丁 numerator「数数者」，出自 numerare「计数」，再上溯到 numerus「数」。数学用法在十六世纪经法语 numérateur 而来。

items.en: Numerus meant 'number'. It is the source of numeral, numerical, enumerate and numerous in English.
items.cn: numerus 意为「数」。它是英语 numeral、numerical、enumerate 与 numerous 的来源。

items.en: Numerare meant 'to count, to number', a verb built directly on the noun.
items.cn: numerare 意为「计数、编号」，是直接由这个名词构成的动词。

items.en: The agent noun numerator named one who counts, a teller or reckoner; the ending -tor marks the person who does the action.
items.cn: 施动名词 numerator 指数数的人，即点算员；词尾 -tor 标记执行动作的人。

items.en: French formed the mathematical term numérateur for the top number of a fraction, since that number counts the parts taken.
items.cn: 法语构成数学术语 numérateur，指分数上方那个数，因为那个数负责清点取走的份数。

items.en: English adopted numerator in the sixteenth century together with the printed notation of fractions.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪随印刷的分数写法一起接受了 numerator。

items.en: The first English citation for the mathematical sense is approximate; numerus and numerare are securely attested Latin words.
items.cn: 数学义在英语中的最早书证为约数；numerus 与 numerare 则是有可靠记录的拉丁词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin word for number and is easily mixed up; the second group names the other parts of a division or ratio.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个表示「数」的拉丁词，容易混淆；第二组是除法或比里的其他部分。

entries.definition: A written sign for a number; it names the mark, not the top part of a fraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指表示数的书写符号；命名的是记号，不是分数的上半部分。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning expressed in numbers; it describes data, not a fraction position.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「用数字表示的」，描述数据，不指分数的位置。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning able to handle numbers, or a verb meaning to count; neither is the fraction term.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词意为「会算数的」，动词意为「计数」；两者都不是分数术语。

entries.definition: To list one by one, from enumerare 'to count out'; it is a verb of listing, not a part of a fraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐项列出，出自 enumerare「数出来」；是列举的动词，不是分数的部分。

entries.definition: The bottom number, built on nomen 'name'; it names the size of the parts while the numerator counts them.
entries.definitionCN: 下面那个数，建立在 nomen「名字」上；它命名每份的大小，而分子负责数份数。

entries.definition: The quantity being divided; in a fraction it is the number above the bar.
entries.definitionCN: 指被除的量；在分数里就是横线上方的数。

entries.definition: The first term of a ratio, matching the numerator's position in a fraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指比的前项，对应分子在分数里的位置。

entries.definition: The number reached by counting; a numerator is that count written above a fraction bar.
entries.definitionCN: 指清点得到的数目；分子就是写成分数横线上方的那个清点结果。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for the numerator used in early teaching.

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: numerus 'number' plus -ator 'one who': the counter, the number that counts the parts.
normal.cn: numerus「数」加 -ator「做……的人」：数数者，负责清点份数的那个数。

normal.en: The family runs numerator, numeral, numerical, numerate and enumerate, all from numerus.
normal.cn: 同族词有 numerator、numeral、numerical、numerate 与 enumerate，都出自 numerus。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: numerator and denominator, common numerator, numerator polynomial.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：分子与分母、公分子、分子多项式。

normal.en: The numerator sits on top and counts; the denominator sits below and names.
normal.cn: 分子在上面负责数，分母在下面负责命名。

normal.en: A percentage is just a fraction with one hundred below, so its top is still a numerator.
normal.cn: 百分数就是分母为一百的分数，所以它的上方仍然是分子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand picking up three slices from a loaf cut into eight.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从切成八片的面包里拿起三片。

abstract.en: Picture a tally keeper standing at the door, marking every person who enters.
abstract.cn: 想象一个记数人站在门口，给每个进来的人画一道。

abstract.en: Picture the number on top of a fraction as a small flag marking how much is claimed.
abstract.cn: 想象分数上面的数是面小旗，标出「要了多少」。

examples.en: When the numerator and denominator share a factor, both can be divided by it.
examples.cn: 分子与分母有公因子时，两边都能被它除。

examples.en: The numerator of the rate counts only confirmed cases.
examples.cn: 这个比率的分子只统计确诊病例。

examples.en: Write the numerator above the bar and the denominator below it.
examples.cn: 把分子写在横线上方，分母写在下方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「数在上」——负责点数的那一行写在上头 → 分子

root: 拉丁 numerus「数」→ numerare「计数」→ numerator「数数者」→ 法语 numérateur（分数上方的数）→ 英语 numerator。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all keep one role: the number that counts what is being taken. It counts slices of a fraction, items in a dividend, the first term of a ratio, cases in a rate, terms of a polynomial and parts of a percentage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个角色：负责清点「取走多少」的那个数。它数分数的份数、被除数里的个数、比的前项、比率中的病例、多项式的项，以及百分数里的份额。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the number written above the fraction bar, marked with red ink.
core.cn: 核心意象：写在分数横线上方的数，被红笔描过。

branches.en: THE COUNTING POSITION: the top number of a fraction, and the shared top number used for comparison.
branches.cn: 计数的位置：分数的上方数，以及用于比较的公分子。

branches.en: THE SAME ROLE ELSEWHERE: the dividend of a division and the first term of a ratio.
branches.cn: 同一角色在别处：除法的被除数与比的前项。

branches.en: COUNTING WHAT HAPPENED: cases in a rate and the share written over one hundred.
branches.cn: 清点发生的事：比率中的病例，以及写在一百上面的份额。

branches.en: POLYNOMIAL ON TOP: algebraic fractions keep the top polynomial in the same seat.
branches.cn: 上面的多项式：代数分式让上方多项式坐同一个位置。

branches.en: THE PERSON WHO COUNTS: the oldest sense, the reckoner with a tally.
branches.cn: 数数的人：最古老的义项，拿筹码清点的人。

intro.en: Numerator is a Latin agent noun on a counting verb; its root and suffix both build a large English family.
intro.cn: numerator 是建立在一个计数动词上的拉丁施动名词；其词根与后缀都构成一个很大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin numerus gives numeral, numerical, numerous and enumerate; the agent suffix -tor gives numerator, denominator and operator.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 numerus 衍生 numeral、numerical、numerous 与 enumerate；施动后缀 -tor 衍生 numerator、denominator 与 operator。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名被数的数。

items.example: The verb supplies the act of counting.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供计数的动作。

items.example: The Latin noun names the person, then the top number.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词先指人，后指上面那个数。

items.example: The data are numerical.

items.meaning: to count; able to use numbers

items.exampleCN: 她懂数且反应快。

items.meaning: to count out one by one

items.exampleCN: 报告逐项列出每笔成本。

items.example: The denominator names the part size.

items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 operator 与 denominator 里。

definition_zh: 许多的；数量众多的；为数不少的
definition_en: existing in large numbers; many in count
core_image: 沙滩上一眼数不完的贝壳一直铺到浪线尽头
scene: 广场上一队接一队的人来登记，志愿者手里的表格翻了一页又一页。Numerous volunteers signed up before noon.
sceneCN: 这里指人数众多（第 2 个义项：人数很多的一群人）；句意为中午之前就有许多志愿者报名；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 许多的；数量众多的

senses.title: A large number of things
senses.definition: a large number of separate countable things
senses.definitionCN: 可单独计数的事物数量很大
senses.example: The shelf holds numerous small boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 架子上放着许多小盒子。
senses.why: Latin numerus meant number and count, and the suffix -osus means full of, so numerous is literally full of number.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 numerus 意为数目与计数，后缀 -osus 意为充满，因此 numerous 字面就是「充满数目」。

senses.title: A great many people
senses.definition: a large body of people
senses.definitionCN: 人数很多的一群人
senses.example: Numerous guests arrived before the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 许多客人在仪式开始前就到了。
senses.why: The adjective is at home with crowds because Latin numerosus described troops as well as things.
senses.whyCN: 这个词与人群天然相合，因为拉丁 numerosus 既描述事物，也描述军队。

senses.title: Many separate occasions
senses.definition: happening on many separate occasions over time
senses.definitionCN: 在时间上分属许多不同场合
senses.example: She raised the point on numerous occasions.
senses.exampleCN: 她在许多场合提出过这一点。
senses.why: Counting moves from objects to events, and the word follows without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 计数从物件转到事件，这个词的形态不变地跟了过去。

senses.title: Many items spread over an area
senses.titleCN: 散布在广大区域内的许多事物
senses.definition: many separate items scattered across a wide area
senses.definitionCN: 许多独立事物散布在广阔区域内
senses.example: The delta contains numerous islands.
senses.exampleCN: 这片三角洲上有众多岛屿。
senses.why: A map shows the count as spread, and the same adjective covers that view.
senses.whyCN: 地图把数量呈现为散落状态，同一个形容词也能覆盖这种视角。

senses.title: Many supporting details
senses.definition: supplied in great quantity, as notes or examples
senses.definitionCN: 以大量注释或例证的形式提供
senses.example: The paper offers numerous examples of the pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文为这一模式提供了大量例证。
senses.why: In academic prose the word counts evidence rather than objects.
senses.whyCN: 在学术写作中，这个词数的是证据，而不是物件。

senses.title: Many reasons in an argument
senses.definition: many points offered in support of a claim
senses.definitionCN: 为支持某一主张而提出的许多论点
senses.example: There are numerous reasons to postpone the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 推迟投票的理由有很多。
senses.why: Debate turns quantity into weight, and the adjective supplies the quantity.
senses.whyCN: 辩论把数量变成分量，这个形容词负责提供数量。

senses.title: A large sample in research
senses.definition: a large count of cases in a study or survey
senses.definitionCN: 研究或调查中大量案例的计数
senses.example: Numerous trials confirmed the effect.
senses.exampleCN: 大量试验确认了这一效应。
senses.why: Statistics needs a plain word for a big count before any test is run.
senses.whyCN: 统计在运行任何检验之前，需要一个表示大计数的平实词。

senses.title: A formal substitute for many
senses.definition: used in formal writing where a bare many would sound abrupt
senses.definitionCN: 用于正式写作，替下显得突兀的「许多」
senses.example: Numerous factors were considered by the board.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会考虑了诸多因素。
senses.why: Register, not meaning, separates numerous from many in much modern use.
senses.whyCN: 在现代用法中，这个词与「许多」的区别多在语体，而非意义。

intro.en: Numerous is Latin numerosus, full of number, built on numerus plus the suffix -osus. The Latin line is clear; the first English date is only approximate.
intro.cn: numerous 来自拉丁 numerosus「充满数目」，由 numerus 加后缀 -osus 构成。拉丁线索清楚，英语首见年代只是约数。

items.en: Numerus meant a number, a count, and also a rank or division; its deeper origin is usually traced to a root meaning to assign or allot.
items.cn: numerus 指数目、计数，也指等级或队列；更深的来源通常追到一个表示「分配」的词根。

items.en: The suffix -osus means full of or abounding in, so numerosus is literally full of number.
items.cn: 后缀 -osus 意为充满、多有，因此 numerosus 字面就是「充满数目」。

items.en: The adjective described things countable in great quantity, especially troops, examples and occasions.
items.cn: 这个形容词描述可大量计数之物，尤用于军队、例证与场合。

items.en: English took the adjective in the sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个形容词，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word survives mainly in formal writing as a polished substitute for many.
items.cn: 这个词主要活在正式写作中，作为 many 的雅致替身。

items.en: Number, numeral, enumerate and numerator all descend from numerus, while numerous is its adjective.
items.cn: number、numeral、enumerate 与 numerator 都出自 numerus，numerous 则是它的形容词。

note.en: The first group descends from the Latin number word; the second group gives plainer ways of saying a large count.
note.cn: 第一组出自拉丁语「数目」一词；第二组是表示「大量」的更平实说法。

entries.definition: A count or total, reaching English through French from Latin numerus.
entries.definitionCN: 计数或总数，经法语从拉丁 numerus 进入英语。

entries.definition: A sign or word for a number.
entries.definitionCN: 表示数目的符号或词。

entries.definition: Expressed in or relating to numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 用数字表示的；与数字有关的。

entries.definition: Able to be counted.
entries.definitionCN: 可以计数的。

entries.definition: A large but unspecified number; plainer than numerous.
entries.definitionCN: 数量大而未指明；比 numerous 更平实。

entries.definition: Too many to count.
entries.definitionCN: 多到数不清。

entries.definition: Present in great quantity, often of supply rather than items.
entries.definitionCN: 大量存在，多指供给而非条目。

entries.definition: A countless or extremely great number, often literary.
entries.definitionCN: 无数或极多，常带文学色彩。

entries.definition: More than two but not a large number.
entries.definitionCN: 多于两个，但数量不算大。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin number word, the real family and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「数目」词、真实同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Numerus is number, and -osus means full of, so numerous means full of numbers.
normal.cn: numerus 是数目，-osus 意为充满，所以 numerous 就是「满是数目」。

normal.en: Number, numeral, enumerate and numerator all come from the same stem.
normal.cn: number、numeral、enumerate 与 numerator 都出自同一词干。

normal.en: The fixed phrase for many occasions marks the time sense.
normal.cn: 表示「在许多场合」的固定说法标出时间义。

normal.en: Numerous replaces many most often in formal writing.
normal.cn: numerous 多在正式写作中替下「许多」这一平实说法。

normal.en: A large sample is described as numerous trials or numerous cases.
normal.cn: 大样本常被说成「大量试验」或「大量案例」。

abstract.en: Numerous is a beach where the shells outnumber the footprints.
abstract.cn: 「众多」是一片沙滩，贝壳比脚印还多。

abstract.en: A count becomes a crowd, and a crowd becomes a weight in an argument.
abstract.cn: 计数变成人群，人群又变成论证里的分量。

abstract.en: The word never says exactly how many, only that counting would take a while.
abstract.cn: 这个词从不说确切多少，只说数起来要花些时间。

examples.en: Numerous small faults appeared along the surface of the beam.
examples.cn: 梁的表面出现了许多细小裂纹。

examples.en: The archive holds numerous letters from the same household.
examples.cn: 档案馆存有这一户人家的许多信件。

examples.en: Numerous attempts failed before the method was found.
examples.cn: 在找到方法之前，已有许多次尝试失败。

branches.en: THE COUNT ITSELF: items large in number, whether stacked or scattered.
branches.cn: 计数本身：数量很大的事物，无论堆叠还是散落。

branches.en: THE CROWD: a large body of people.

senses.title: A person trained to care for the sick
senses.definition: A person trained to care for the sick
senses.definitionCN: 照护病人的专业人员
senses.example: The nurse checked his pulse.

definition_en: a place where young children are cared for, a place where young plants are raised and sold, and by extension any place that shelters early growth
core_image: 玻璃棚下一排排嫩苗舒展开叶片，等着一双粗糙的手把它们移进大田
scene: 三月清晨的温室里，一位老花农把刚冒芽的小苗一株株移进木箱。Before the last frost, he moved every seedling into a warm nursery.
sceneCN: 这里的 nursery 是「苗圃」（第 2 个义项：培育并出售幼苗的地方）；句意为在最后一场霜来临前，他把每株幼苗都搬进了温暖的苗圃。图中可辨识物件：玻璃棚、木箱、嫩苗。

pos.zh: 托儿所；育婴室；苗圃；培养地

由 nurse 与 maid 复合而成，义为「保姆；照看孩子的女佣」
由 nursery 与 man 复合而成，义为「苗圃经营者；花木培育者」

senses.title: A place where young children are cared for
senses.definition: a room or small building where babies and very young children are looked after while their parents are at work
senses.definitionCN: 父母上班时照看婴儿和幼儿的房间或小建筑
senses.example: The baby spends the morning at a nursery near the office.
senses.exampleCN: 宝宝上午在办公室附近的一家托儿所度过。
senses.why: The word grew from nurse, the person who feeds and tends a child, and the -ery ending names a place, so a nursery is first of all where nursing happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从 nurse（喂养并照看孩子的人）长出来，-ery 后缀标出一个场所，所以 nursery 首先是「照护发生的地方」。

senses.title: A place where young plants are raised
senses.definition: a place, often with glasshouses, where young plants are grown and sold to gardeners
senses.definitionCN: 通常带有温室的场所，在那里培育幼苗并出售给园艺爱好者
senses.example: She bought a small apple tree from a local nursery.
senses.exampleCN: 她从当地一家苗圃买了一棵小苹果树。
senses.why: Nursing is not only for children: the same care applied to weak young plants produced this sense, because a nursery is wherever early life is kept alive.
senses.whyCN: 照护不只针对孩子：把同样的呵护用在娇弱的幼苗上，就生出这个义项，因为苗圃正是让早期生命存活下来的地方。

senses.title: A place or environment that develops talent
senses.definition: a place or environment where a particular kind of person, skill or idea is developed early and protected
senses.definitionCN: 某类人、技能或想法早期得到发展并受到保护的地方或环境
senses.example: The small club became a nursery for young musicians.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小俱乐部成了年轻音乐人的培养地。
senses.why: Once a nursery is a sheltered place for beginnings, any institution that raises talent early can borrow the word, so schools and clubs use it too.
senses.whyCN: 既然 nursery 指为「开端」提供庇护的场所，任何早早培养人才的机构都能借这个词，于是学校与俱乐部也用它。

senses.title: A child's room in an old-fashioned house
senses.definition: a room in a house, especially an old-fashioned one, where the children sleep and play
senses.definitionCN: 宅子里供孩子睡觉和玩耍的房间，尤指老式住宅中的儿童房
senses.example: The old house still had a nursery with a rocking chair.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老宅里还留着一间放着摇椅的儿童室。
senses.why: Before public care existed, looking after small children was a room inside the home, so the place meaning of -ery turned inward and named a domestic room.
senses.whyCN: 在公共托育出现之前，照看幼儿只是宅子里的一间房，于是 -ery 的「场所」义指向室内，命名了一间家庭用房。

intro.en: Nursery is an English formation from nurse plus the place suffix -ery; nurse itself goes back through Old French to Latin words for nourishing.
intro.cn: nursery 是英语用 nurse 加场所后缀 -ery 造出的词；nurse 本身经古法语上溯到拉丁语中表示「滋养」的词。

items.en: Nutrire meant to feed, suckle and nourish, and it described the bodily care given to the very young.
items.cn: nutrire 意为喂养、哺乳、滋养，描述的是给予幼小者的身体照料。

items.en: A nutrix was a wet nurse, the woman who fed and tended another woman's baby, so the word carried both feeding and caring.
items.cn: nutrix 指乳母，即喂养并照看别人家婴儿的女子，这个词同时带着「喂」与「护」两层意思。

items.en: Old French norrice kept the sense of a woman who suckles and cares for a child, and English borrowed it as nurse.
items.cn: 古法语 norrice 保留了「哺乳并照看孩子的女子」这一意思，英语借入后写作 nurse。

items.en: English added -ery, a suffix for a place or a collective activity, so nursery named the place where nursing was done.
items.cn: 英语加上表示场所或一类活动的后缀 -ery，于是 nursery 命名了「照护发生的场所」。

items.en: Modern English spread nursery from the child's room to the childcare centre and then to the garden, where young plants receive the same tending.
items.cn: 现代英语让 nursery 从孩子的房间扩展到托育机构，再扩展到花园，在那里幼苗得到同样的照料。

note.cn: 形近组收建立在 nurse 之上的词；近义组收照看幼儿或培育幼苗的场所。

normalIntro.en: Nursery is nurse turned into a place, and the -ery suffix keeps the idea of a spot set aside for care.
normalIntro.cn: nursery 是把 nurse 变成场所的说法，-ery 后缀保留了「专门划出来照护的一处地方」这个意思。

normal.en: Nurse means to feed and tend, and -ery means a place, so nursery is literally a tending place.
normal.cn: nurse 意为喂养和照看，-ery 意为场所，所以 nursery 字面上就是「照看的地方」。

normal.en: Nursery school and day nursery keep the child-care sense: one for older toddlers, one for babies.
normal.cn: nursery school 与 day nursery 都保留育儿义：一个收较大的幼儿，一个收婴儿。

normal.en: Plant nursery moved the same care outdoors, because seedlings need shelter as much as infants do.
normal.cn: plant nursery 把同一种照料搬到户外，因为幼苗和婴儿一样需要庇护。

normal.en: Nursery rhyme survives from the old sense of a child's room, where such songs were sung.
normal.cn: nursery rhyme 保留了「孩子的房间」这个旧义，那些歌谣正是在那里唱的。

normal.en: Nurseryman adds man to nursery, naming the person who tends plants in such a place.
normal.cn: nurseryman 在 nursery 后加 man，指出在这个场所里照看植物的人。

abstract.en: A nursery is a protected interval in the life of something small, before it must face the open field.
abstract.cn: 苗圃是一样小东西生命中被保护起来的一段时间，之后它才必须面对开阔的田野。

abstract.en: One word for babies and seedlings suggests that early growth, human or green, asks for the same conditions.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时指婴儿和幼苗，说明无论是人还是植物，早期生长都需要相似的条件。

abstract.en: Calling a club a nursery admits that talent, like a seedling, needs a sheltered first season.
abstract.cn: 把一个俱乐部称作 nursery，就是承认才能也像幼苗一样，需要有一个受庇护的第一季。

examples.en: This nursery sells young fruit trees in spring.

examples.en: That little theatre was a nursery for several famous actors.

definition_zh: 养分；营养素
definition_en: a substance that provides nourishment and is needed by a living thing for growth and health
core_image: 植物的根系伸向土壤颗粒，旁边一盘食物被分成几块不同颜色的区域
scene: 这里指「养分」。 Nitrogen is the nutrient that limits plant growth in most temperate soils.
sceneCN: 这里 nutrient 指「限制性养分」（第 3 个义项：生态学中供应最不足、决定生长上限的那种养分）；温带土壤里最缺的往往是氮，它因此限制了植物生长。图中可辨识物件：植物根系、土壤颗粒、氮标记、生长曲线。

pos.zh: 养分；营养素（可数，如 essential nutrients）
提供养分的；营养的（多作定语，如 nutrient-rich）

senses.title: A substance that nourishes
senses.titleCN: 养分：为生命提供养料的东西
senses.definition: any substance that an organism takes in and uses to build tissue or obtain energy
senses.definitionCN: 生物摄入并用于构建组织或获取能量的任何物质
senses.example: Every cell needs a steady supply of nutrients.
senses.exampleCN: 每个细胞都需要稳定的养分供应。
senses.why: The word is the present participle of Latin nutrire 'to nourish', so a nutrient is literally 'a nourishing thing'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是拉丁 nutrire「滋养」的现在分词，因此 nutrient 字面就是「正在滋养的东西」。

senses.title: Essential nutrients in food
senses.titleCN: 必需营养素：人体不能自己合成的成分
senses.definition: the dietary components, such as vitamins, minerals, amino acids and fatty acids, that the body cannot make in sufficient amounts
senses.definitionCN: 维生素、矿物质、氨基酸与脂肪酸这类人体无法足量自造的膳食成分
senses.example: Vitamin C is an essential nutrient for humans.
senses.exampleCN: 维生素 C 是人体的一种必需营养素。
senses.why: Nutrition separates what the body can synthesise from what it must eat, and calls the second group essential.
senses.whyCN: 营养学把身体能合成的与必须从食物摄入的分开，称后者为「必需」。

senses.title: Limiting nutrient in ecology
senses.titleCN: 限制性养分：决定生长上限的那一种
senses.definition: in ecology, the nutrient in shortest supply relative to demand, which caps growth until it is added
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中指相对需求供应最不足的养分，在补充它之前一直限制生长
senses.example: Phosphorus is often the limiting nutrient in freshwater lakes.
senses.exampleCN: 磷常常是淡水湖泊中的限制性养分。
senses.why: Ecologists name the bottleneck rather than the whole list, so 'limiting nutrient' became a single fixed phrase.
senses.whyCN: 生态学家命名的是瓶颈而非整张清单，因此「限制性养分」成了一个固定短语。

senses.title: Plant nutrients
senses.titleCN: 植物养分：氮磷钾等矿质元素
senses.definition: the mineral elements that plants absorb from soil or water, especially nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium
senses.definitionCN: 植物从土壤或水中吸收的矿质元素，尤其是氮、磷、钾
senses.example: The fertiliser supplies the three main plant nutrients.
senses.exampleCN: 这种肥料提供三种主要的植物养分。
senses.why: Agriculture lists nutrients by element because a plant's needs can be measured as ions taken from soil.
senses.whyCN: 农业按元素列出养分，因为植物的需求可以按从土壤吸收的离子来衡量。

senses.title: Absorption and deficiency
senses.titleCN: 吸收与缺乏：临床上的养分供应
senses.definition: in medicine, a nutrient as something absorbed by the gut or lacking in a patient's diet
senses.definitionCN: 医学中指被肠道吸收、或在患者膳食中缺乏的养分
senses.example: The disease blocks nutrient absorption in the small intestine.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病阻碍小肠吸收养分。
senses.why: Clinical usage focuses on the path from food to cell, so the word appears in absorption and deficiency alike.
senses.whyCN: 临床用法关注从食物到细胞的路径，因此这个词在「吸收」与「缺乏」两种语境里都出现。

senses.title: Nutrient pollution
senses.titleCN: 养分污染：过量营养物进入水体
senses.definition: in environmental science, nitrogen and phosphorus entering water in excess and triggering algal blooms
senses.definitionCN: 环境科学中指过量的氮与磷进入水体并引发藻华
senses.example: Nutrient pollution from farms turned the bay green.
senses.exampleCN: 农场带来的养分污染让海湾变绿。
senses.why: The same substances that are food on land become pollution in water, so the neutral word gains a negative use.
senses.whyCN: 在陆地上是食物的同一物质，在水里成了污染，因此这个中性词获得了负面用法。

senses.title: Nutrient-rich as an adjective
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe something that supplies nutrients, as in nutrient-rich soil or nutrient solution
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，描述提供养分的事物，如富含养分的土壤或营养液
senses.example: The delta's nutrient-rich silt feeds the rice fields.
senses.exampleCN: 三角洲富含养分的淤泥滋养着稻田。
senses.why: English lets nouns modify nouns, so the same word describes a medium without changing form.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许名词作定语，因此同一个词不需变形就能描述某种介质。

senses.title: Nutrient medium in the lab
senses.titleCN: 营养培养基：培养微生物的配方
senses.definition: in microbiology, the prepared mixture of nutrients used to grow cells or bacteria in culture
senses.definitionCN: 微生物学中指用于培养细胞或细菌的配制养分混合物
senses.example: The bacteria grew well on the nutrient agar.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌在营养琼脂上长得很好。
senses.why: Laboratory practice turns the general word into a countable product name, as in nutrient agar and nutrient broth.
senses.whyCN: 实验室实践把这个泛称变成可数的产品名，如营养琼脂与营养肉汤。

intro.en: Nutrient is the English form of Latin nutriens, the present participle of nutrire 'to nourish, to suckle'.
intro.cn: nutrient 是拉丁 nutriens 的英语形式，即动词 nutrire「滋养、哺乳」的现在分词。

items.en: Latin nutrire meant 'to nourish, to feed, to suckle'. It is the source of nutrition, nutritious, nourish and nurse.
items.cn: 拉丁 nutrire 意为「滋养、喂养、哺乳」。它是 nutrition、nutritious、nourish 与 nurse 的来源。

items.en: The form nutriens, nutrient- meant 'nourishing, the thing that nourishes', and English took it as an adjective and later as a noun.
items.cn: 形式 nutriens、nutrient- 意为「滋养的、滋养之物」，英语先把它作形容词，后来才作名词。

items.en: English nutrient is recorded as an adjective in the sixteenth century, meaning 'nourishing', in medical and botanical writing.
items.cn: 英语 nutrient 在 16 世纪作为形容词有记录，意为「滋养的」，见于医学与植物学著作。

items.en: The noun use, meaning 'a nourishing substance', became common in the nineteenth century with the rise of nutritional science.
items.cn: 名词用法「滋养物质」在 19 世纪随营养科学的兴起而普及。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology and agriculture extended the noun to soil, water and fertiliser, producing phrases such as limiting nutrient.
items.cn: 20 世纪的生态学与农业把这一名词扩展到土壤、水与肥料，产生了「限制性养分」这类短语。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation of nutrient is uncertain; the adjective and noun dates overlap, and the shift from one to the other is not documented in a single text.
items.cn: 来源不确定：nutrient 的英语首见确切书证年代存疑；形容词与名词的用法年代相互交叠，从前者转为后者的过程并无单一文献记录。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same Latin family that answer different grammatical questions; the second holds words for what is eaten or added.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族、但回答不同语法问题的词；第二组指被吃掉或被添加的东西。

entries.definition: The process of being nourished, or the scientific study of it. A nutrient is the substance; nutrition is the process and the field.
entries.definitionCN: 被滋养的过程，或研究它的学科。nutrient 是物质，nutrition 是过程与学科。

entries.definition: Describes food that is rich in nutrients, as in a nutritious meal. It judges the food, not the substance.
entries.definitionCN: 描述富含养分的食物，如「有营养的一餐」。它评价食物，而不是物质本身。

entries.definition: Means 'relating to nutrition', as in nutritional value. It frames a topic, while nutritious makes a judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与营养有关的」，如营养价值。它框定话题，而 nutritious 作出评价。

entries.definition: The food or support that keeps something alive and growing. It stresses the effect of being fed rather than the chemical identity.
entries.definitionCN: 维持生命与生长的食物或支持。它强调被喂养的效果，而非化学身份。

entries.definition: Any substance eaten to sustain life. Food contains nutrients, but a food is the whole item, not one component.
entries.definitionCN: 为维持生命而摄入的任何物质。食物含有养分，但食物是整体，不是某一成分。

entries.definition: A product taken to add a nutrient that the diet may lack. It is a delivery format, not a category of nutrient.
entries.definitionCN: 为补充膳食可能缺乏的养分而服用的产品。它是供给形式，而不是养分类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin nutrire 'nourish' + -ent: the nourishing thing.
normal.cn: 拉丁 nutrire「滋养」+ -ent：正在滋养的东西。

normal.en: The family runs nutrition, nutritional, nutritious, nourish, nourishment and malnutrition.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 nutrition、nutritional、nutritious、nourish、nourishment、malnutrition。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: essential nutrients, nutrient cycling, limiting nutrient, nutrient pollution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：必需营养素、养分循环、限制性养分、养分污染。

normal.en: A nutrient is a substance; nutrition is the process; nutritious describes the food.
normal.cn: nutrient 是物质，nutrition 是过程，nutritious 描述食物。

normal.en: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium are the three main plant nutrients.
normal.cn: 氮、磷、钾是三种主要的植物养分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a root hair drawing a charged particle from a soil grain.

branches.en: GENERAL: any substance that builds tissue or supplies energy.
branches.cn: 泛指：任何构建组织或提供能量的物质。

branches.en: HUMAN BODY: what cannot be made must be eaten, absorbed and delivered.
branches.cn: 人体：不能自造的就必须吃进、吸收并送达。

branches.en: ECOLOGY: the scarcest nutrient caps growth, and a rich medium is described by the same word.
branches.cn: 生态：最稀缺的养分决定生长上限，而富含养分的介质也用同一个词描述。

branches.en: AGRICULTURE: nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium are counted as the main plant nutrients.
branches.cn: 农业：氮、磷、钾被算作主要的植物养分。

branches.en: EXCESS AND CULTURE: too much in a river is pollution; the right mix in a dish grows microbes.
branches.cn: 过量与培养：河里太多是污染，皿里配好则培养微生物。

intro.en: Nutrient is a Latin participle used unchanged in English, so its ending -ent marks 'the one doing the nourishing'.
intro.cn: nutrient 是原样进入英语的拉丁分词，词尾 -ent 标记「正在做滋养这件事的一方」。

latinIntro.en: Latin nutrire supplied the whole family: nutriens as participle, nutritio as action noun, and nutritius as adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 nutrire 提供了整族词：分词 nutriens、动作名词 nutritio 与形容词 nutritius。

definition_zh: 营养；营养学
definition_en: the process by which living things obtain and use the food they need, and the scientific study of that process

pos.zh: 营养；营养学（多作不可数名词；指学科时为不可数）

senses.title: The process of being nourished
senses.titleCN: 营养过程：摄入与利用食物的全过程
senses.definition: the whole process by which an organism takes in food and uses it for energy, growth and repair
senses.definitionCN: 生物摄入食物并把它用于能量、生长与修复的全过程
senses.example: Nutrition begins with chewing and ends inside every cell.
senses.exampleCN: 营养从咀嚼开始，到每个细胞为止。
senses.why: The Latin action noun names an activity, not a substance, so nutrition is first of all something that happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动作名词命名的是活动而非物质，因此 nutrition 首先是一件正在发生的事。

senses.title: The scientific discipline
senses.titleCN: 营养学：研究食物与健康的学科
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies nutrients, how the body uses them and how diet affects health
senses.definitionCN: 研究养分、身体如何利用它们以及膳食如何影响健康的科学分支
senses.example: She studied nutrition before working in public health.
senses.exampleCN: 她在进入公共卫生领域之前学的是营养学。
senses.why: Because the process is complex enough to study, the same noun came to name the academic field without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 由于这一过程复杂到值得研究，同一个名词不需变形就成了一门学科的名字。

senses.title: The quality of a diet
senses.titleCN: 膳食质量：一个人实际获得的营养
senses.definition: the nourishment a person or population actually receives through their diet, judged as good or poor
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体通过膳食实际获得的营养，可评为良好或不足
senses.example: Good nutrition in early childhood pays off for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 幼儿期良好的营养会在几十年后仍然受益。
senses.why: Clinicians and policy makers speak of nutrition as a state to be assessed, so the process word also names a condition.
senses.whyCN: 临床医生与政策制定者把营养当作可评估的状态，因此过程词也指一种状况。

senses.title: Clinical nutrition
senses.titleCN: 临床营养：以营养手段治疗患者
senses.definition: the medical specialty that manages diet, tube feeding and intravenous feeding in illness
senses.definitionCN: 在疾病中管理膳食、管饲与静脉营养的医学专科
senses.example: The clinical nutrition team adjusted his tube feed.
senses.exampleCN: 临床营养团队调整了他的管饲配方。
senses.why: When eating is impossible, nutrition becomes a medical intervention with doses and protocols.
senses.whyCN: 当无法进食时，营养就变成有剂量与规程的医疗干预。

senses.title: Plant nutrition
senses.titleCN: 植物营养：根系吸收与光合作用
senses.definition: in botany, the way plants obtain mineral ions from soil and carbon from the air
senses.definitionCN: 植物学中指植物从土壤取得矿质离子、从空气取得碳的方式
senses.example: Plant nutrition depends on both root uptake and photosynthesis.
senses.exampleCN: 植物营养同时依赖根系吸收与光合作用。
senses.why: Botanists reuse the word for a completely different strategy, because the goal of obtaining matter for growth is the same.
senses.whyCN: 植物学家把这个词用于完全不同的策略，因为「获取物质以生长」这一目标是相同的。

senses.title: Public health nutrition
senses.titleCN: 公共营养：人群层面的膳食政策
senses.definition: the population-level field that shapes food supply, fortification and dietary advice
senses.definitionCN: 在人群层面塑造食物供应、营养强化与膳食建议的领域
senses.example: Public health nutrition cut iodine deficiency across the country.
senses.exampleCN: 公共营养工作在全国范围内减少了碘缺乏。
senses.why: The unit of study shifts from a body to a population, and the word scales up with it.
senses.whyCN: 研究对象从个体身体转为整个人群，这个词也随之放大。

senses.title: On the packet
senses.titleCN: 营养标签：包装上的营养成分
senses.definition: the nutrient information printed on food packaging, often headed nutrition facts
senses.definitionCN: 食品包装上印制的养分信息，常以「营养成分表」为标题
senses.example: The nutrition label lists sugar per serving.
senses.exampleCN: 营养标签列出每份的糖含量。
senses.why: Regulation turned the science into a standard table, so the word appears on every packet.
senses.whyCN: 法规把这门科学变成标准表格，因此这个词出现在每个包装上。

senses.title: Nutrition transition
senses.titleCN: 营养转型：人群膳食结构的改变
senses.definition: the shift in a population's diet toward processed food, sugar and fat as incomes rise
senses.definitionCN: 随着收入提高，人群膳食向加工食品、糖与脂肪转变的过程
senses.example: The country's nutrition transition brought rising obesity.
senses.exampleCN: 该国的营养转型带来了肥胖率上升。
senses.why: Epidemiologists needed a name for a society-wide change, so they extended the word with 'transition'.
senses.whyCN: 流行病学家需要为全社会层面的变化命名，便给它加上了 transition。

intro.en: Nutrition comes from Latin nutritio, an action noun from nutrire 'to nourish'. English adopted it in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: nutrition 出自拉丁 nutritio，是动词 nutrire「滋养」构成的行动名词，英语在 16 世纪借入。

items.en: Latin nutrire meant 'to nourish, to suckle'. Its family includes nutriens 'nourishing' and nutritius 'nourishing, nutritious'.
items.cn: 拉丁 nutrire 意为「滋养、哺乳」，其同族词包括 nutriens「滋养的」与 nutritius「有营养的」。

items.en: The action noun nutritio, nutritionis named the act of feeding and the state of being fed, in medical and philosophical Latin.
items.cn: 行动名词 nutritio、nutritionis 在医学与哲学拉丁文中指喂养的动作与被滋养的状态。

items.en: Old French nutrition passed into English in the sixteenth century, first as a medical term for the body's uptake and use of food.
items.cn: 古法语 nutrition 在 16 世纪进入英语，最初是医学术语，指身体摄取与利用食物。

items.en: In the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries the word became the name of a discipline, as calories, vitamins and deficiency diseases were described.
items.cn: 19 世纪至 20 世纪初，随着热量、维生素与缺乏病被描述，这个词成了一门学科的名称。

items.en: Later in the twentieth century nutrition entered policy language through fortification programmes, school meals and labelling rules.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期，营养经强化计划、学校供餐与标签规则进入政策语言。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation of nutrition is uncertain, usually given as the 1550s but not fixed; the earliest uses are translations of Latin medical texts.
items.cn: 来源不确定：nutrition 的英语首见确切书证年代存疑，通常写作 16 世纪 50 年代但并不确定；最早用例是拉丁医学文献的译本。

note.en: The first group holds same-family words that divide the topic differently; the second holds words for what is eaten, how much is eaten, and whether it is enough.
note.cn: 第一组是同族词，但把话题切分得不同；第二组指吃的东西、吃的量以及是否足够。

entries.definition: A single nourishing substance such as a vitamin or an amino acid. Nutrition is the process and the field that study many nutrients together.
entries.definitionCN: 单一种滋养物质，如某种维生素或氨基酸。nutrition 是过程，也是把多种 nutrient 放在一起研究的学科。

entries.definition: An adjective praising food as rich in nutrients. It evaluates a meal, while nutrition names a process or a science.
entries.definitionCN: 称赞食物富含养分的形容词。它评价一餐，而 nutrition 命名过程或学科。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'relating to nutrition', as in nutritional value. It labels the dimension being discussed.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与营养有关的」的形容词，如营养价值。它标明讨论的是哪个维度。

entries.definition: The material or support that keeps something alive. It is more concrete and emotional than the clinical word nutrition.
entries.definitionCN: 维持生命所需的物质或支持。它比临床味更重的 nutrition 更具体、更有情感色彩。

entries.definition: The usual food a person or group eats, or a planned restriction. Nutrition is what the body does with that diet.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或群体常吃的食物，或计划性的限制饮食。nutrition 是身体对这份膳食做了什么。

entries.definition: Poor nutrition caused by too little food or by an unbalanced diet. It is the failure case of nutrition, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 因食物不足或膳食失衡造成的营养不佳。它是营养的反面情形，而非同义词。

definition_zh: 营养的；营养方面的
definition_en: relating to nutrition, or to the nutrients contained in a food
core_image: 一个被放大的食品标签，上面的成分表被红笔圈出
scene: 这里指「营养的」。 The nutritional value of the flour fell when the bran was removed.
sceneCN: 这里 nutritional 指「营养价值的」（第 2 个义项：食物所含养分的数量与质量）；去掉麸皮后，面粉的营养价值随之下降。图中可辨识物件：面粉袋、放大镜、营养成分表、红笔圈注。

pos.zh: 营养的；营养方面的（多作定语，如 nutritional value）

senses.title: Relating to nutrition
senses.titleCN: 与营养有关：泛指这一领域
senses.definition: concerning nutrition as a process or a field, without naming a specific value
senses.definitionCN: 涉及营养这一过程或领域，但不指名具体的数值
senses.example: The clinic offers nutritional advice for young mothers.
senses.exampleCN: 该诊所为准妈妈提供营养建议。
senses.why: The suffix -al turns the noun into a general adjective of relation, the same pattern as nation to national.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把名词变成表示关系的泛形容词，nation 变 national 也是同一模式。

senses.title: Nutritional value
senses.titleCN: 营养价值：食物所含养分的数量与质量
senses.definition: the amount and quality of nutrients a food provides per unit, often per serving or per hundred grams
senses.definitionCN: 食物每单位（常按份或每百克）提供的养分数量与质量
senses.example: Refining removes much of the grain's nutritional value.
senses.exampleCN: 精加工去掉了谷物的大部分营养价值。
senses.why: Value language lets nutrition be compared and priced, so the adjective attaches to a measurable quantity.
senses.whyCN: 用「价值」这一说法能让营养被比较与计价，因此这个形容词常附着于可测量的量。

senses.title: Nutritional deficiency
senses.titleCN: 营养缺乏：某种养分长期不足
senses.definition: a state caused by too little of one or more nutrients over time, producing specific symptoms
senses.definitionCN: 长期缺乏一种或多种养分造成的状态，会产生特定症状
senses.example: Iron deficiency is the commonest nutritional deficiency worldwide.
senses.exampleCN: 缺铁是全世界最常见的营养缺乏。
senses.why: Medicine labels the cause rather than the symptom, so a disease such as anaemia is traced back to a nutritional deficiency.
senses.whyCN: 医学命名的是原因而非症状，因此贫血这类疾病会被追溯到营养缺乏。

senses.title: Nutritional status
senses.titleCN: 营养状况：个体整体的营养水平
senses.definition: the overall condition of a person's body as judged by weight, growth, blood markers and diet
senses.definitionCN: 通过体重、生长、血液指标与膳食判断的个人身体整体状况
senses.example: The survey mapped the nutritional status of schoolchildren.
senses.exampleCN: 该调查描绘了学龄儿童的营养状况。
senses.why: Public health needs one phrase for the combined result of many measurements, so 'status' is added to the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生需要用一个短语概括多项测量的综合结果，因此在形容词后加上 status。

senses.title: Nutritional supplements and therapy
senses.definition: products or treatments that supply nutrients missing from the diet or unavailable through eating
senses.definitionCN: 补充膳食中缺失、或因无法进食而不能获得的养分的产品或治疗
senses.example: She took a nutritional supplement during pregnancy.
senses.exampleCN: 她在孕期服用了一种营养补充剂。
senses.why: The adjective marks the purpose, separating a nutrient product from a drug with a different action.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标明用途，把营养产品与作用机制不同的药物区分开。

senses.title: Nutritional labelling
senses.titleCN: 营养标签标注：法规要求的成分披露
senses.definition: the regulated declaration of nutrient content on food packaging
senses.definitionCN: 法规要求在食品包装上披露养分含量
senses.example: Nutritional labelling made sugar content impossible to hide.
senses.exampleCN: 营养标签标注让糖含量无处隐藏。
senses.why: Regulators name the panel after the adjective, so the word appears on every packet as a legal category.
senses.whyCN: 监管者以这个形容词命名标签，因此它作为法律类别出现在每个包装上。

senses.title: Nutritional requirements
senses.titleCN: 营养需求：维持健康所需的量
senses.definition: the amounts of each nutrient needed daily for health, set by expert committees
senses.definitionCN: 专家委员会设定的、每日维持健康所需的各养分数量
senses.example: The feed was formulated to meet the birds' nutritional requirements.
senses.exampleCN: 饲料按禽类的营养需求配制。
senses.why: Once needs are quantified, they become requirements, and the adjective ties them to nutrition rather than to appetite.
senses.whyCN: 一旦需求被量化，它就成了「要求」，而这个形容词把它与营养而非食欲联系起来。

senses.title: Nutritional ecology
senses.titleCN: 营养生态学：食物质量如何影响动物
senses.definition: the study of how the nutrient content of food shapes the behaviour, health and distribution of animals
senses.definitionCN: 研究食物的养分含量如何塑造动物行为、健康与分布
senses.example: Nutritional ecology explains why deer choose young shoots.
senses.exampleCN: 营养生态学解释了鹿为何选择嫩枝。
senses.why: Ecology borrows the adjective to study food quality rather than mere quantity, giving it a research field of its own.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借这个形容词研究食物质量而非仅有数量，从而形成一个独立研究领域。

intro.en: Nutritional is nutrition plus the adjective ending -al, from Latin -alis. The noun itself comes from Latin nutritio.
intro.cn: nutritional 是 nutrition 加形容词词尾 -al，后者出自拉丁 -alis。名词本身则来自拉丁 nutritio。

items.en: Latin nutrire 'to nourish, to suckle' is the ultimate source, and it also gives nutrient, nourish and nurse.
items.cn: 拉丁 nutrire「滋养、哺乳」是最终来源，它也给出 nutrient、nourish 与 nurse。

items.en: The action noun nutritio 'a feeding, nourishment' supplied the French and English noun nutrition.
items.cn: 行动名词 nutritio「喂养、营养」提供了法语与英语的 nutrition。

items.en: The adjective ending -alis meant 'relating to' and became English -al, visible in national, natural and nutritional.
items.cn: 形容词词尾 -alis 意为「与……有关」，变为英语 -al，可见于 national、natural 与 nutritional。

items.en: As nutrition became a science, English formed nutritional to describe values, deficiencies and requirements. The exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 随着营养成为一门科学，英语造出 nutritional 来描述价值、缺乏与需求。最早的确切年代存疑。

items.en: The adjective spread into food law and ecology, producing fixed terms such as nutritional labelling and nutritional ecology.
items.cn: 这个形容词扩散到食品法规与生态学，产生了营养标签标注、营养生态学等固定术语。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the first English use of nutritional is not securely dated, and it may have appeared independently in medical and agricultural writing.
items.cn: 来源不确定：nutritional 的英语首见年代没有可靠定论，它可能在医学与农业文献中各自独立出现。

note.en: The first group holds adjective and noun forms from the same family that are constantly interchanged; the second holds adjectives describing food quality.
note.cn: 第一组是同族但常被互换的形容词与名词形式；第二组是描述食物质量的形容词。

entries.definition: Means 'rich in nutrients' and praises the food. Nutritional merely labels the dimension, as in nutritional value.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「富含养分的」，带有对食物的称赞。nutritional 只是标明维度，如营养价值。

entries.definition: The noun for the process or the science. Nutritional is the adjective built from it.
entries.definitionCN: 表示过程或学科的名词。nutritional 是由它构成的形容词。

entries.definition: The countable substance, as in essential nutrients. Nutritional describes a property of a whole food.
entries.definitionCN: 可数的物质，如必需营养素。nutritional 描述整个食物的一种属性。

entries.definition: A near synonym meaning 'serving as nourishment', still used in animal science, as in nutritive value.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「起滋养作用的」近义词，仍用于动物科学，如营养价值。

entries.definition: Relating to the diet as a whole, as in dietary fibre. It frames intake, while nutritional frames nutrient content.
entries.definitionCN: 与整体膳食有关，如膳食纤维。它框定摄入，而 nutritional 框定养分含量。

entries.definition: Describes food or living that is good for health, often with a moral or traditional overtone that nutritional lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 描述有益健康的食物或生活，常带道德或传统色彩，而 nutritional 没有这层意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: nutrition + -al: relating to nutrition.
normal.cn: nutrition + -al：与营养有关的。

normal.en: The family runs nutrition, nutritionist, nutritionally, nutritious, nutrient and malnutrition.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 nutrition、nutritionist、nutritionally、nutritious、nutrient、malnutrition。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: nutritional value, nutritional status, nutritional supplement, nutritional labelling.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：营养价值、营养状况、营养补充剂、营养标签标注。

normal.en: nutritional labels a dimension; nutritious praises the food.
normal.cn: nutritional 标明维度，nutritious 称赞食物。

normal.en: Removing bran lowers flour's nutritional value, which is why wholemeal is preferred.
normal.cn: 去掉麸皮会降低面粉的营养价值，这也是全麦更受青睐的原因。

abstract.cn: 想象一个被放大的标签，上面一张数字表格，其中一行被红笔圈出。

abstract.en: Picture two loaves side by side, one dark and dense, one pale and airy.
abstract.cn: 想象两条面包并排，一条深色紧实，一条浅色松软。

abstract.en: Picture a child's growth chart where the line flattens for a year and then climbs again.
abstract.cn: 想象一张儿童生长图，曲线平了一年，然后又向上走。

examples.en: Wholemeal bread has a higher nutritional value than white bread.
examples.cn: 全麦面包的营养价值高于白面包。

examples.en: The team assessed the children's nutritional status before the programme.
examples.cn: 项目开始前，团队评估了儿童的营养状况。

examples.en: Nutritional labelling is mandatory on most packaged foods.
examples.cn: 多数包装食品必须标注营养标签。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nutrition（营养）+ al（的）」——与营养有关的 → nutritional 营养的

root: 拉丁 nutrire「滋养」→ nutritio → nutrition；加拉丁 -alis（英语 -al）→ nutritional。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses show one adjective doing different jobs: framing a topic, pricing a food, naming a deficiency, describing a person, a product, a label, a requirement and a research field.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项展示同一个形容词的不同职务：框定话题、给食物定价、命名缺乏、描述个人、产品、标签、需求与一个研究领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a magnified food label with one row circled in red.
core.cn: 核心意象：被放大的食品标签，其中一行被红笔圈出。

branches.en: GENERAL FRAME: -al simply says the topic is nutrition.
branches.cn: 泛框定：-al 只是说话题属于营养。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: value and requirements turn nutrients into numbers to compare and prescribe.
branches.cn: 计量：价值与需求把养分变成可比较、可规定的数字。

branches.en: CLINICAL PICTURE: a deficiency is named, and a person's overall state is assessed.
branches.cn: 临床图景：命名一种缺乏，并评估一个人的整体状态。

branches.en: REMEDY: supplements and therapy fill the gap that diet leaves.
branches.cn: 补救：补充剂与治疗填上膳食留下的缺口。

branches.en: LAW AND RESEARCH: labels are regulated, and ecology studies food quality.
branches.cn: 法规与研究：标签受监管，生态学研究食物质量。

intro.en: Nutritional is a Latin action noun with a Latin relational ending, so the whole word says 'pertaining to nourishment'.
intro.cn: nutritional 是拉丁行动名词加拉丁关系词尾，整个词的意思就是「与滋养相关的」。

latinIntro.en: Latin -alis gives English -al; the stem comes from nutritio, itself from nutrire.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 -alis 给出英语 -al；词干来自 nutritio，而 nutritio 又出自 nutrire。

definition_zh: 肥胖症；肥胖；体脂过多
definition_en: a medical condition in which excess body fat has accumulated to the point that it may harm health
core_image: 体重秤的指针压过红色刻度，腰腹堆起一圈厚厚的脂肪
scene: 社区体检的早晨，护士把软尺绕在一位中年男子的腰上，读数明显偏大。The nurse explained that obesity increases the risk of diabetes and heart disease.
sceneCN: 这里 obesity 是「肥胖症」（第 1 个义项：体脂过量并可能损害健康的疾病）；句意：护士解释说，肥胖症会增加糖尿病和心脏病的风险。

pos.zh: 肥胖症；肥胖（体脂过多的状态）

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「肥胖的」，是 obesity 的词干来源，指体脂多到影响健康
由本词 obesity 加后缀 -genic 构成，义为「致肥胖的」，形容促使人发胖的环境或食物
由本词 obesity 加后缀 -gen 构成，义为「致肥胖物质」，指被认为会促进肥胖的化学因素
由前缀 anti- 加本词构成，义为「抗肥胖的」，多用于药物与政策名称

senses.title: A clinical condition of excess body fat
senses.titleCN: 肥胖症：体脂过量的临床疾病
senses.definition: a medical condition in which excess body fat has accumulated enough to impair health, usually assessed by body mass index
senses.definitionCN: 体脂堆积到足以损害健康的疾病状态，通常用体重指数评估
senses.example: Obesity is diagnosed when the body mass index reaches thirty.
senses.exampleCN: 体重指数达到三十时即可诊断为肥胖症。
senses.why: The Latin noun obesitas named fatness; medicine turned that descriptive word into a diagnosable condition with measured thresholds.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 obesitas 本指「肥胖」，医学把这个描述性词变成可用指标界定的可诊断疾病。

senses.title: The visible state of being very overweight
senses.titleCN: 肥胖：体态上的体脂过多
senses.definition: the state of carrying much more body fat than is typical for a person of the same height and build
senses.definitionCN: 与同身高体型的人相比体脂明显过多的状态
senses.example: Her obesity made walking uphill difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 她的肥胖让上坡行走变得吃力。
senses.why: Before it was a diagnosis, the word simply described a body that had eaten itself fat, so the state sense stays closest to the original image.
senses.whyCN: 在成为诊断之前，这个词只是描述一个「吃得把自己养肥」的身体，所以状态义最贴近原初意象。

senses.title: A public health burden
senses.definition: the widespread rise of excess body fat in a population, treated as a collective public health problem
senses.definitionCN: 人群中体脂过量现象普遍上升，被视为集体性的公共卫生问题
senses.example: Childhood obesity has become a public health burden in many cities.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童肥胖在许多城市已成为公共卫生负担。
senses.why: When millions of bodies gain fat at once, the personal state becomes a collective trend that health systems must measure and manage.
senses.whyCN: 当千百万人同时发胖，个人的状态就变成卫生系统必须测量和管理的集体趋势。

intro.en: Obesity comes from Latin obesitas, meaning fatness, built on obedere, to eat away or overeat, from ob- over and edere to eat.
intro.cn: obesity 来自拉丁语 obesitas「肥胖」，由 obedere「吃掉、吃得过多」构成，其中 ob- 表「过度」，edere 表「吃」。

items.en: Edere means to eat, and it is the root behind edible and the participle obesus.
items.cn: edere 意为「吃」，是 edible 与分词 obesus 背后的词根。

items.en: Ob plus edere yields obesus, literally eaten fat, used of a person or body that is corpulent. The force of ob- here is usually taken as over or intensive.
items.cn: ob 与 edere 合成 obesus，字面是「被吃肥的」，用来形容肥胖的人或身体。这里的 ob- 一般认为表「过度」或起加强作用。

items.en: The abstract noun obesitas names fatness or corpulence, and it is the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: 抽象名词 obesitas 指肥胖或肥满，是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.en: French obésité is usually cited as a parallel route into educated English, alongside direct borrowing from Latin.
items.cn: 一般认为法语 obésité 是进入英语的另一条路径，与直接借自拉丁语的情况并存。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English from the early seventeenth century, at first as a general word for fatness.
items.cn: 这个名词自十七世纪初见于英语记录，最初只是泛指肥胖。

items.en: Twentieth-century medicine gave it a measured definition through body mass index, and public health made it a global epidemic.
items.cn: 二十世纪的医学用体重指数给它一个可测量的定义，公共卫生则把它变成全球性的流行问题。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adjective and the technical compounds built on the same Latin root; the near-meaning group holds words for excess weight that come from other roots.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词根构成的形容词与技术复合词；近义组收来自其他词根的「体重过多」说法。

entries.definition: very fat in a way that harms health; the adjective behind obesity
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「肥胖的」，指体脂多到影响健康，是 obesity 的词干来源

entries.definition: describing an environment or food that promotes weight gain
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「致肥胖的」，形容促使人发胖的环境或食物

entries.definition: a chemical or other factor thought to promote obesity
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「致肥胖物质」，指被认为会促进肥胖的化学物质或其他因素

entries.definition: weighing more than is healthy; a broader and less clinical term than obesity
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「超重」，比 obesity 更宽泛，临床色彩更弱

entries.definition: the amount or degree of body fat, especially as measured in medicine
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「脂肪蓄积度」，尤指医学测量中的体脂量

entries.definition: the state of being fat; an older and more formal word
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肥胖」，是较古老、较正式的说法

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root, the adjective family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根、形容词词族，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Ob- means over and edere means to eat: to become obese is to eat past what the body needs.
normal.cn: ob- 表「过度」，edere 表「吃」：变胖就是吃得超过了身体所需。

normal.en: The adjective is obese, and the suffix -ity turns it into obesity, just as active becomes activity.
normal.cn: 形容词是 obese，后缀 -ity 把它变成 obesity，正如 active 变成 activity。

normal.en: Childhood obesity is the phrase used when the weight problem begins early in life.
normal.cn: childhood obesity 指体重问题在生命早期就开始出现。

normal.en: Morbid obesity is the medical label for the most severe class, where the risk is highest.
normal.cn: morbid obesity 是对最严重等级的医学称呼，此时风险最高。

normal.en: An obesogenic environment makes the healthy choice the harder one.
normal.cn: obesogenic environment 指让健康选择变得更难的环境。

abstract.en: Picture a clinic scale whose needle passes the red mark while the nurse writes a diagnosis.
abstract.cn: 想象诊所的体重秤指针越过红色刻度，护士在一旁写下诊断。

abstract.en: Picture a belt that has to be let out one notch after another.
abstract.cn: 想象腰带一格一格地往外放。

abstract.en: Picture a city map on which fast-food signs outnumber playgrounds.
abstract.cn: 想象一张城市地图，快餐招牌比操场还多。

examples.en: Obesity raises the risk of diabetes and heart disease.
examples.cn: 肥胖症会增加糖尿病和心脏病的风险。

examples.en: The clinic runs a twelve-week programme for patients with obesity.
examples.cn: 这家诊所为肥胖症患者开设了一个十二周的项目。

examples.en: Childhood obesity has risen sharply in many countries.
examples.cn: 儿童肥胖在许多国家急剧上升。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧比西提」——听上去像「哦，必死体」，只是谐音玩笑。真正的线索是 ob-（过度）+ edere（吃）：吃得过多，身体把脂肪存成了病。谐音不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 ob-（过度、越过）+ edere（吃）→ obesus（被吃肥的）→ obesitas（肥胖）→ 英语 obesity；核心义是「吃得过多，身体把多余能量存成脂肪」。ob- 在此一般认为表「过度」或起加强作用。

sensesIntro.en: Obesity begins as a measured clinical condition, extends to the visible state of a fat body, and finally names a collective public health trend.
sensesIntro.cn: obesity 从可测量的临床疾病出发，扩展到身体脂肪过多的可见状态，最后指集体的公共卫生趋势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale needle passing the red mark while fat gathers at the waist.
core.cn: 核心意象：体重秤指针越过红色刻度，脂肪堆在腰腹。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: body mass index turns fatness into a diagnosis with fixed thresholds.
branches.cn: 诊室线：体重指数把肥胖变成有固定界值的诊断。

branches.en: THE BODY: the visible state of carrying far more fat than the frame expects.
branches.cn: 身体线：身体承载的脂肪远超骨架所需，这是可见的状态。

branches.en: THE POPULATION: millions of such bodies make obesity a public health burden.
branches.cn: 人群线：千百万个这样的身体让肥胖成为公共卫生负担。

branches.en: The diagnosis measures what the body already shows.
branches.cn: 诊断测量的正是身体早已呈现的状态。

branches.en: A personal state becomes a collective trend when it spreads across a population.
branches.cn: 个人状态在人群中蔓延时，就变成集体趋势。

intro.en: Obesity is a Latin noun built from a prefix of excess and the verb for eating; English adds the adjective obese and technical compounds.
intro.cn: obesity 是由表「过度」的前缀与表示「吃」的动词构成的拉丁名词；英语再加 obese 及技术复合词加以扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin edere means to eat; ob- adds the idea of over or across, and obesus is its participle, eaten fat.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 edere 意为「吃」；ob- 加上「过度、越过」之意，obesus 是其分词，意为「被吃肥的」。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of excess to the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给动词加上「过度」的意思。

items.example: Edere is the eating root shared by edible.
items.exampleCN: edere 是与 edible 共有的「吃」词根。

items.example: Obesus describes a body that has eaten itself fat.
items.exampleCN: obesus 形容一个被吃得肥起来的身体。

items.example: Obesitas is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: obesitas 是英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix turns obese into obesity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 obese 变成 obesity。

items.example: Obese is the adjective that names the condition.
items.exampleCN: obese 是描述这种状态的形容词。

items.example: The suffix forms obesogenic.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 obesogenic。

items.example: An obesogenic environment favours cheap, dense food.
items.exampleCN: 致肥胖环境偏爱廉价而热量密集的食物。

items.example: Obesogens are studied as possible chemical triggers.
items.exampleCN: obesogens 被研究为可能的化学诱因。

items.example: It forms anti-obesity drugs.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 anti-obesity 这类药物名称。

definition_zh: 物体；物品；对象；目的；宾语；反对
definition_en: a thing that can be seen and touched; also the focus of attention or an aim, a grammatical noun that receives the action of a verb, and, as a verb, to express disagreement
core_image: 一件可以拿在手里的东西，被托到眼前，也随时能挡回去
scene: 清晨的库房里，管理员把收到的旧物一件件摆上长桌，登记重量与年份。The curator lifted each object and wrote its weight in a notebook.
sceneCN: 这里 object 是「物体、物品」（第 1 个义项：能看见、能拿起来的实物）；句意为管理员拿起每一件器物，把重量记在本子上。图中可辨识物件：长桌、旧物、笔记本。

pos.zh: 物体；物品；对象；目的；宾语
反对；提出异议

derivatives.zh: 由 object 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「反对；异议」
由 object 加 -ive 构成，义为「目标；客观的」
由 objective 加 -ity 构成，义为「客观性」
由 object 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -or 构成，义为「反对者」
由 objection 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「令人反感的；可反对的」

senses.title: A thing that can be seen and touched
senses.definition: a solid thing that exists in the physical world and can be seen or handled
senses.definitionCN: 存在于物质世界、能看见或拿在手里的实体
senses.example: A small object rolled under the table and stopped at her feet.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小东西滚到桌下，停在她脚边。
senses.why: Latin objectum names what has been thrown before the eyes, so the physical thing is the first thing this word ever pointed at.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 objectum 指「被抛到眼前的东西」，所以能看见的实物是这个词最初指向的对象。

senses.title: The focus of attention or feeling
senses.definition: a person or thing toward which attention, interest or a feeling is directed
senses.definitionCN: 注意力、兴趣或情感所指向的人或物
senses.example: The old house became the object of every photographer's attention.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老房子成了每个摄影师关注的对象。
senses.why: Once something is thrown before the mind, it can hold the mind there; the physical thing turns into whatever attention is aimed at.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西既然被抛到心里，就能把心思留住；实物于是转成「注意力瞄准的那个东西」。

senses.title: An aim that a plan is meant to reach
senses.definition: the aim that a plan or an action is meant to achieve
senses.definitionCN: 计划或行动想要达到的那一点
senses.example: The committee met with the object of cutting waiting times.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会开会，目的是缩短等候时间。
senses.why: An aim is also something placed in front of you to move toward, so the word shifts from what is looked at to what is worked for.
senses.whyCN: 目标也是放在你前方、要你走过去的东西，于是词义从「被看着的物」转到「为之努力的终点」。

senses.title: The noun that receives a verb's action
senses.definition: in grammar, the noun or pronoun that the action of a verb is done to
senses.definitionCN: 语法上，承受动词动作的名词或代词
senses.example: In the sentence she wrote the letter, the noun letter is the object.
senses.exampleCN: 在「她写了那封信」这句话里，名词 letter 是宾语。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word because the object is the thing placed before the verb's action, receiving what is done to it.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用这个词，因为宾语正是被放到动词动作前面的东西，承受着被做的动作。

senses.title: To say that you disagree
senses.definition: to say that you do not agree with or approve of something
senses.definitionCN: 表示不同意或不赞成某事
senses.example: Several neighbours objected to the plan for a new car park.
senses.exampleCN: 好几位邻居反对新建停车场的方案。
senses.why: Latin obicere meant to throw something against someone, and an objection is a word thrown back at a proposal; the modern verb keeps that gesture of standing in the way.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obicere 意为把东西朝某人扔过去，而反对就是把一句话扔回给一个提议；这个现代动词保留了「挡在前面」的动作。

intro.en: Object comes from Latin words for throwing something before or against; the same root splits into a noun for what is placed in view and a verb for speaking against it.
intro.cn: object 来自拉丁语「把东西抛到前面或对着扔」的说法；同一条词根分成两支，一支指摆在眼前的物，一支指对着说的反对。

items.en: Jacere meant to throw or to cast, and it lies under the -ject of many English words.
items.cn: jacere 意为投、掷，它藏在许多英语词的 -ject 一段里。

items.en: Obicere joined ob-, against or in front of, with jacere, so it meant to throw something in someone's way and also to throw a charge against a person.
items.cn: obicere 把表示对着、在前面的 ob- 与 jacere 合起来，意为把东西抛到某人面前，也指对某人提出责难。

items.en: Objectum, the thing thrown before the mind, came to name whatever is presented to thought, and later the target of a feeling or an aim.
items.cn: objectum 指被抛到心里的东西，用来指呈现在思想面前的一切，后来又指情感或目标所指向的靶子。

items.en: Old French took object as something perceived or opposed, and English borrowed it with both a noun and a verb in view.
items.cn: 古法语把这词用作「被感知之物」与「被反对之物」，英语借用时就同时看到了名词与动词两条路。

items.en: Modern English separates the two by stress: the noun keeps the first syllable strong, the verb moves the beat to the end, and grammar adds the sense of a verb's object.
items.cn: 现代英语用重音把两者分开：名词重音在前，动词重音挪到后面；语法上又添出「动词宾语」一义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same -ject stem from jacere; the near-meaning group gathers words for physical things and for speaking against something.
note.cn: 形近组收同一条 jacere 词干上的 -ject 词；近义组收表示实物与出言反对的词。

entries.definition: A statement or feeling of disagreement.
entries.definitionCN: 表示不同意的话或情绪；异议。

entries.definition: An aim, or something judged without personal feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 目标，或不受个人情感影响的。

entries.definition: A planned piece of work, or to throw something forward.
entries.definitionCN: 有计划的工作，或向前投射。

entries.definition: To put a liquid into the body with a needle.
entries.definitionCN: 用针把液体注入体内。

entries.definition: Any physical item or matter.
entries.definitionCN: 任何实物或东西。

entries.definition: One separate article in a list or a set.
entries.definitionCN: 列表或成套物品中单独的一件。

entries.definition: To say publicly that something is wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 公开表示某事不对。

entries.definition: To speak or act against a plan or an idea.
entries.definitionCN: 出言或行动反对某个计划或想法。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb for throwing, so every sense is some version of something placed in front of someone.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词长在表示「投掷」的拉丁动词上，所以每个义项都是「某样东西被放到某人面前」的某种变形。

normal.en: Jacere is Latin for throw, and the -ject in object, project and inject all comes from it.
normal.cn: jacere 在拉丁语里是投掷，object、project、inject 里的 -ject 都出自它。

normal.en: Object and objection share one root, but object names the thing in front of you while objection names the words thrown back.
normal.cn: object 与 objection 同根，但 object 指摆在眼前的物，objection 指扔回去的话。

normal.en: The noun takes the stress on the first syllable and the verb on the second, a split English made to keep the two jobs apart.
normal.cn: 名词把重音放在第一音节，动词放在第二音节，这是英语为了把两件事分开而做的切分。

normal.en: With the object of is a fixed phrase meaning with the aim of, because an object can be a goal.
normal.cn: with the object of 是固定说法，意为以……为目的，因为 object 可以是目标。

normal.en: Object to is followed by a noun or an -ing form, because the preposition to blocks the plain infinitive.
normal.cn: object to 后面接名词或动名词，因为介词 to 挡住了光秃秃的不定式。

abstract.en: Anything you can point at, anything you aim at, and anything you say against a plan are all, in this word, something placed in front of you.
abstract.cn: 你能指着的东西、你瞄准的东西、你对着计划说的话，在这个词里都是「被放到你面前的东西」。

abstract.en: The same root that throws a stone in someone's path also throws a thought before the mind.
abstract.cn: 同一条词根，既把石头扔到别人路上，也把一个念头扔到心里。

abstract.en: A word that names both a pebble and a protest shows how often disagreement begins with simply seeing something in the way.
abstract.cn: 一个既能指小石子、又能指抗议的词，说明不赞同常常始于「看见有东西挡在路上」。

examples.en: A small object rolled under the table and stopped at her feet.
examples.cn: 一个小东西滚到桌下，停在她脚边。

examples.en: Several neighbours objected to the plan for a new car park.
examples.cn: 好几位邻居反对新建停车场的方案。

examples.en: The committee met with the object of cutting waiting times.
examples.cn: 委员会开会，目的是缩短等候时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥不借它」——东西递到眼前偏说不借；object 既是眼前之物，也是出言反对。

root: 一般认为来自拉丁语 objectum（被抛到眼前之物），源于 obicere（对着投掷），由 ob-（对着）加 jacere（投掷）构成，经古法语 object 进入英语；名词与动词重音不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something thrown in front of you; from that one gesture come the physical thing, the target of attention, the aim in view, the grammatical receiver and the words spoken against a plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被抛到你面前的东西」；同一个动作长出实物、注意力的靶子、眼前的目标、语法上的承受者，以及对着计划说出的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a solid thing held up before the eyes, and a hand raised to push it away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件实物被托到眼前，随即有一只手把它推回去。

branches.en: a small thing rolling out of sight under a table
branches.cn: 小东西滚到桌下看不见的地方

branches.en: an old house drawing every camera in the street
branches.cn: 一座老房子引来街上所有的镜头

branches.en: a meeting called to shorten the wait at a stop
branches.cn: 为缩短站上等候时间而开的会

branches.en: the noun that takes what the verb does
branches.cn: 承受动词动作的那个名词

branches.en: neighbours standing up to speak against a plan
branches.cn: 邻居们站起来反对一个方案

intro.en: The word is Latin ob- plus jacere, and its English branch grows through endings that turn the stem into a noun of action and an adjective of judgement.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语的 ob- 加 jacere，它的英语分支靠后缀长成表示动作的名词与表示判断的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin jacere, to throw, and its compounds obicere and objectum are the recorded source of this word, whose stem also underlies project and inject.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jacere（投掷）及其复合词 obicere、objectum 是这个词语有记录的来源，它的词干也支撑着 project 与 inject。
